Specify a union-formation process

Source: R/union_formation.R
union_formation.Rd

Construct or attach a union-formation specification without executing it. In on-demand mode, at a birth use the woman's current partner, or choose a partner from all living, unpartnered men using conditional-logit probabilities from the matching formula to form a union. Men below min_male_age are excluded. If no eligible man exists, cancel the birth by default; cancel_birth_if_no_match = FALSE preserves it with unknown father. Known kin within kinship_generations on both sides of a common ancestor are excluded. Each person may have only one ongoing union. Partnered men are not available; surviving husbands return to the pool at widowhood. Death ends affected unions. In rate mode unpartnered women face competing search events and use their unpartnered fertility schedule and may give birth without initiating a search. Failed searches draw another waiting time; formation and widowhood switch fertility schedules while preserving spacing. An overall fertility schedule applies to both statuses, with a simulation warning. On-demand mode requires an overall fertility schedule. Unpartnered rate-mode births use the same eligibility and exact draw to assign a father, using father_matching when supplied or otherwise matching, without forming a union or removing him from availability. A search with no eligible man cancels the birth by default. No previous-father preference is applied.

Usage

union_formation(
  initiation,
  matching = create_age_gap_matching_model(0, 5),
  rates = NULL,
  min_male_age = 15,
  kinship_generations = 2,
  father_matching = NULL,
  cancel_birth_if_no_match = TRUE,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  group_prop_hazard = NULL,
  cohab_prob = NULL,
  cohab_matching = NULL,
  union_convert_rate = NULL,
  cohabitation_counts_as_previous_union = FALSE
)

set_union_formation(
  model,
  initiation,
  matching = create_age_gap_matching_model(0, 5),
  rates = NULL,
  min_male_age = 15,
  kinship_generations = 2,
  father_matching = NULL,
  cancel_birth_if_no_match = TRUE,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  group_prop_hazard = NULL,
  cohab_prob = NULL,
  cohab_matching = NULL,
  union_convert_rate = NULL,
  cohabitation_counts_as_previous_union = FALSE
)

Arguments

initiation

Either "on_demand" for birth-triggered searches or "rate" for scheduled searches. No default is selected.

matching

A specification created by create_matching_model(), or a tibble with numeric time_start, time_end, and list-column model holding complete matching objects. Model intervals are half-open absolute years, cannot overlap, and must cover the requested run. The active model is used at partner selection, without changing pending search dates or existing unions. Base data frames with list columns are also accepted. Defaults to create_age_gap_matching_model(0, 5): preferred age gap zero years, with selection weight halving five years on either side.

rates

For "rate" initiation, an age-specific female search-hazard table with age_start, age_end, and rate, in years and per person-year. These specify search attempts, not guaranteed realized union formation. An optional group column selects the woman's group. Without it, all groups share the schedule. Group does not restrict partner matching. With no population groups, simulation warns and selects the first alphabetical group. See mortality() for group-label and rate-coverage rules. Nonoverlapping bands may have gaps or an open end; gaps and ages outside support have zero hazard. Optional previous_union supplies either "none", "separated", "widowed", or pooled "none", "dissolved". Dissolved pools separation and widowhood. Each group and active calendar slice must supply one complete set; mixing the sets is not allowed. Without it, the schedule applies to all previous union types. Categories describe the most recent recorded episode; complete histories are required. Optionally include both dur_start and dur_end for elapsed years since the most recent union ended. Each row supplies either age or duration bands with both unused boundaries NA. none must use age; each other category uses one clock consistently across all its bands and groups. Age and duration cannot apply together. All-age inputs may omit duration columns. Must be NULL for "on_demand".

min_male_age

Minimum male age in continuous years at a new partner search, default 15. Finite nonnegative scalar; zero disables this age exclusion. Existing unions are retained. No minimum is added for actual female event eligibility. Weighted choice counts unpartnered men and women at or above this same cutoff when calibrating its weights.

kinship_generations

Generation bound on both sides of a known common ancestor, default 2. Excludes parents, grandparents, siblings, aunts/uncles, nieces/nephews and first cousins, including half relationships, when known. Zero imposes no cross-person kin exclusion. Missing ancestry is not proof of unrelatedness; only demonstrated relationships are screened. Existing unions are retained. See extract_kin() for the shared distance definitions.

father_matching

Optional matching specification for fathers of unpartnered births in rate mode, created by create_matching_model(), or a time_start/time_end/model schedule as for matching. Defaults to NULL, using the general matching model active at that birth. Union searches always use matching. Not used by on-demand initiation. Process-level age and kinship screening settings are shared; NULL inherits the general model's settings.

cancel_birth_if_no_match

Logical, default TRUE. Cancel a birth when its on-demand partner search or rate-mode nonmarital father selection fails. Set FALSE to allow births with unknown fathers. Historical missing father IDs are retained. A cancellation starts no new spacing interval and draws fresh waiting times from the failed attempt. Partner scarcity can reduce realized fertility below inputs.

diagnostics

Logical, default FALSE. When the general matching model uses weighted choice in a grouped population, record .log_weight_<group> columns on newly formed unions: the log group weights applied at the search that formed each union (0 for the reference group and when calibration cannot affect choices). Use the column for each alternative's group as a conditional-logit offset in wife-side choice sets.

group_prop_hazard

Optional named numeric vector of finite nonnegative search-rate multipliers by the woman's group. Missing groups use 1.0; zero suppresses searches. Applies to shared or group-specific input rates. Without population groups, simulation warns and ignores multipliers. Requires initiation = "rate"; on-demand formation has no search hazard. Matching utilities and input rate tables are unchanged.

cohab_prob

Optional age-specific probability table with age_start, age_end, prob, optionally group and previous_union. Enables typed unions only in rate mode. Age gaps mean zero. Optional time_start and time_end supply half-open calendar intervals; each active slice must satisfy the same age/group/previous-category rules and cover the run. Type uses the active probability at the search instant, before matching. Existing unions keep their types. NULL retains untyped partnerships and their RNG path.

cohab_matching

Optional cohabitation matching model or whole-model schedule; NULL shares the general matching model active at that search. Marriage, cohabitation and unpartnered father searches calibrate weights using their own intensities and share the available male pool.

union_convert_rate

Optional age- or duration-specific conversion table, optionally by woman's group. Duration uses the current cohabitation start. Uses rate and either age or duration boundaries, not both clocks, with no previous-union axis. NULL gives no conversions and warns at simulation. Conversion keeps partners, closes cohab with reason conversion, and starts a linked marriage with a new dissolution-duration origin.

cohabitation_counts_as_previous_union

Logical, default FALSE. FALSE restores previous legal-marriage category after a cohabitation ends; TRUE classifies cohab breakup/death as separated/widowed. Search duration still starts at the latest partnership ending. Only applies to typed unions.

model

A hammel_model object.

Value

union_formation() returns a hammel_union_formation process; set_union_formation() returns an updated model. Rate tables are tibbles.

Details

Partners are drawn exactly from the full conditional-logit distribution over all eligible men, without a candidate sample. Living, unpartnered men are grouped by group and quarter-year birth bin; a bin is chosen in proportion to its size times the largest weight any member could have, a member is accepted with the ratio of his weight to that maximum, and only he is screened for age and kinship. For the built-in linear/quadratic age model this is exact. Custom R formulas are bounded on a 1/32-year grid; if a drawn man's utility exceeds the bound, simulation warns that draws were approximate. Existing unions are retained even if a new-search restriction would exclude the partner.

Matching always uses calibrated male-group weights: a woman chooses among screened candidates with each man's selection weight multiplied by a weight for his group. Weights are recalculated at every search, in continuous time, so that expected male union flows by group match a mirrored target: each unpartnered man has the per-capita intensity of an unpartnered woman of his group, adjusted by the matching model's delta. Women's intensity is the search hazard for rate-mode searches and the unpartnered fertility hazard (zero during birth spacing) for on-demand searches and nonmarital father selection, which has its own weights and uses the father model's preferences and delta when one is supplied. Weights depend only on the man's group, so they do not change the association between partners' characteristics in the static group-only illustration. With one group, all group weights are one. When no exact weights exist, approximate weights are used with a warning.

Calendar rates

Search rates and union_convert_rate optionally accept time_start and time_end for half-open absolute calendar-year bands, including fractional years. Both columns are required together, with finite starts and greater ends (possibly Inf). Every active slice must satisfy its existing rate rules and cover the requested run. Clock choices stay consistent across periods; changes precede same-time events and retain duration origins. cohab_prob accepts the same calendar columns, with probabilities selected at the search instant. Probability-only changes refresh matching calibration without resampling pending event clocks. All three matching arguments also accept whole-model schedule tibbles with time_start, time_end, and list-column model. Model changes update role-specific preferences and calibration before same-time choices without resampling event clocks. All supplied models, including future intervals, are validated; gaps in a run are errors. NULL father/cohabitation matching dynamically follows general matching. Other non-rate arguments remain static.
